newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Monte Carlo firm buys Cumnock stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Monte Carlo firm buys Cumnock stake.

text.p: Steaming coal miner Cumnock Coal Ltd said on Monday that an unlisted firm with addresses in the Bahamas and Monte Carlo had acquired a 9.6 percent stake.
Cumnock company secretary Nick Geddes told Reuters that the unlisted firm, Dafen Ltd, had told the Australian Stock Exchange it owned three million shares.
Geddes said most of the shares had been bought from Tom Johnson, who suddenly resigned as chairman last Wednesday.
His 2.4 million shares were sold two days later, along with another 600,000 shares, at A$2.40 per share.
Geddes said he did not know why Johnson, who was also managing director had resigned.
The board of directors would meet later on Monday to consider the appointment of new executives, he said.
Swiss commodities group Glencore Ag is the largest shareholder in Cumnock, whose operations are based in the Hunter Valley north of Sydney, with a 25.14 percent stake.
Its holding was acquired under a hostile bid earlier in 1996 pitched at A$2.50 per share.
More recently, CIM Resources Ltd ended merger talks with Cumnock, dropping the share price to $1.80.
Cumnock shares were five cents higher at A$2.45 in light turnover at 2.10 p.m. (0310 GMT).
